Converts lines to a raster: the cells crossed by a line get its value, the others are novalue.

**Toolbox folder:** Raster Processing<br>
**Status:** Certified<br>
**Keywords:** Raster, Vector, Lines, Rasterize<br>
**Authors:** Andrea Antonello<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.modules.LinesRasterizer`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inVector` | vector file |  |  | The lines to rasterize. |
| `fCat` | String |  |  | The optional numeric field of the lines with the value of their cells. |
| `pCat` | double |  | `1.0` | The value of the cells if no field is given. |
| `inRaster` | raster file |  |  | An optional raster that gives the grid, instead of bounds, rows and columns. |
| `pNorth` | Double |  |  | The north bound of the region to consider |
| `pSouth` | Double |  |  | The south bound of the region to consider |
| `pWest` | Double |  |  | The west bound of the region to consider |
| `pEast` | Double |  |  | The east bound of the region to consider |
| `pRows` | Integer |  |  | The rows of the region to consider |
| `pCols` | Integer |  |  | The cols of the region to consider |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outRaster` | output file |  | The rasterized lines. |

**Notes**

Every segment of the lines becomes the chain of cells that joins the cells of its two vertices, with the Bresenham algorithm: the chain is 8-connected, one cell wide, as a path of the flow directions, so a rasterized network can be used where the network extracted from the elevation would be. A segment that touches a cell only on a corner can leave it out. Where lines cross, the cell keeps the largest value, as the higher order of two streams that join. The parts of the lines outside of the grid are left out.

The value of the cells is the one of the numeric field of the line, or the constant category without a field. The grid is the one of the optional raster, or the one of the bounds, rows and columns.
